\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{برنده} \fa{شدن} (barande shodan)}{برنده شدن (barande shodan)}]{\fa{برنده} \fa{شدن} (barande shodan) — to win}

\label{lesson:FA-C343-barande-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a parade, then the Persian for joy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{برنده} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{برنده} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{barande shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to win\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تیم} \fa{ما} \fa{در} \fa{مسابقه} \fa{برنده} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tim-e mâ dar mosâbeqe barande shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our team won the match.
\end{quote}

\emph{barande} \textquotedblleft{}a winner\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{bordan} \textquotedblleft{}to carry off, to win\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{barande mishavad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{barande} \textquotedblleft{}a winner\textquotedblright{} is built on \emph{bar-}, the present stem of the native verb \emph{bordan} \textquotedblleft{}to carry off, to win\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-ande} \textquotedblleft{}one who\textquotedblright{}; \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} is inherited too.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barande shodan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barande shodan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{barande shodan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a parade, then the Persian for joy, then say \emph{barande shodan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{باختن} (bâkhtan)}{باختن (bâkhtan)}]{\fa{باختن} (bâkhtan) — to lose (a game)}

\label{lesson:FA-C343-bakhtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for joy, then the Persian for to win.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{باختن}}
\textbf{\fa{باختن}} (\emph{bâkhtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to lose (a game)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تیم} \fa{ما} \fa{دو} \fa{بر} \fa{یک} \fa{باخت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tim-e mâ do bar yek bâkht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our team lost two to one.
\end{quote}

Present stem \emph{bâz-}: \emph{mibâzad}. For losing a thing Persian says \emph{gom kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâkhtan} is a native Persian verb with the present stem \emph{bâz-}, the same shape as in \emph{bâzi} \textquotedblleft{}game\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâkhtan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bâkhtan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bâkhtan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for joy, then the Persian for to win, then say \emph{bâkhtan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{باختن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To lose (a game)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تماشاگر} (tamâshâgar)}{تماشاگر (tamâshâgar)}]{\fa{تماشاگر} (tamâshâgar) — a spectator}

\label{lesson:FA-C343-tamashagar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to win, then the Persian for to lose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تماشاگر}}
\textbf{\fa{تماشاگر}} (\emph{tamâshâgar}) — \textquotedblleft{}a spectator\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تماشاگران} \fa{تا} \fa{آخر} \fa{بازی} \fa{ماندند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tamâshâgarân tâ âkhar-e bâzi mândand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The spectators stayed until the end of the game.
\end{quote}

\emph{tamâshâ} \textquotedblleft{}watching\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-gar}. Plural \emph{tamâshâgarân}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tamâshâgar} adds the Persian suffix \emph{-gar} to \emph{tamâshâ} \textquotedblleft{}watching, a show\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB derives from the Arabic verb \emph{mashā} \textquotedblleft{}to walk\textquotedblright{}, so first a stroll about, then a show.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to win, then the Persian for to lose, then say \emph{tamâshâgar} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تشویق} \fa{کردن} (tashviq kardan)}{تشویق کردن (tashviq kardan)}]{\fa{تشویق} \fa{کردن} (tashviq kardan) — to cheer (on); to encourage}

\label{lesson:FA-C343-tashviq-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to lose, then the Persian for a spectator.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تشویق} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تشویق} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tashviq kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to cheer (on); to encourage\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تماشاگران} \fa{تیم} \fa{را} \fa{تشویق} \fa{کردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tamâshâgarân tim râ tashviq kardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The spectators cheered the team on.
\end{quote}

Also \textquotedblleft{}to encourage\textquotedblright{}: \emph{marâ be khândan tashviq kard}. Present \emph{tashviq mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tashviq} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{tashwīq}, \textquotedblleft{}a stirring of desire, an encouragement\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مدال} (medâl)}{مدال (medâl)}]{\fa{مدال} (medâl) — a medal}

\label{lesson:FA-C343-medal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a spectator, then the Persian for to cheer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مدال}}
\textbf{\fa{مدال}} (\emph{medâl}) — \textquotedblleft{}a medal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{در} \fa{مسابقه} \fa{مدال} \fa{طلا} \fa{گرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U dar mosâbeqe medâl-e talâ gereft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She won a gold medal in the competition.
\end{quote}

\emph{Medâl-e noqre} is silver, \emph{medâl-e boronz} bronze.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{medâl} is usually traced to French \emph{médaille}, \textquotedblleft{}medal\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
